# Chapter 02 - Responsibility Position

The final page needed a signer.

Signing a full name would give the court someone to punish. Leaving the space empty would let future readers treat the page as a stray note.

The investigator drew two small marks outside the main text.

Not a name.

A position.

The marks sat beside the cut line, close enough to say someone had stood here, far enough that no living helper could be pulled out by name.

"Will they understand it?" the clerk asked.

"Not always," she said. "But without it, they will not even know where to ask."

The clerk brought an old seal with the family mark worn flat.

"Half a print," he said. "Enough to show this page was placed, not enough to name a house."

The ink touched only the corner.

The investigator added one sentence under the marks:

One record may not decide a death alone.

The sentence looked cold. That was why it could survive.

When she carried the page into the modern review room, the screen did not find her full name. It found the space where her method should have been anonymous.

The system suggested an exceptional association.

Her chair moved half a step away from the primary reviewer line.
